Ok builders, here’s your playbook. Prototype your product with the best frontier model. Cost be damned. Validate the user experience. Then, 6-8 weeks later when open-weight models catch up - move your production workloads there, and to smaller models where possible. In that order. Don’t start with the cheapest model.

Pinned: The best model for early product validation is almost never the best model for production. Talked to a bunch of founders this weekend. There’s a standard playbook emerging : 1/ Prototype with the best frontier models. Max quality. Ignore cost and latency. Learn what users actually want and iterate. 2/ Once the workflow and UX is validated, optimize like crazy for cost and latency - prompt eng, model routing, harnesses, smaller models, fine tuning. I see most teams get stuck in step 1.
